- Enemies learn your strategies: if you always fight with fire, they develop fire resistance; if you sneak, they get better hearing; if you run, they chase farther.

Controls: WASD move, mouse aim, click attack, Space dodge, E interact, Tab memory, C craft, Shift sprint. Mobile touch joystick + buttons.

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

The runtime prompt is a generic FPS prompt, not this user's. We just need to build a game matching the pitch.

Plan: build "THE WORLD REMEMBERS" — a browser survival game with persistent adaptive memory. Single-page, no build step (index.html + modules). Use Canvas 2D with high-quality rendering. Must be mobile-friendly.

Let me design deeply but keep implementation manageable.

## Core fantasy
You wake in a valley that has been watching. Every run leaves scars: enemies evolve resistances/tactics, NPCs remember your kindness or cruelty, the land remembers where you burned and built. Death is permanent for the run, but the world persists across runs (localStorage).

## Gameplay
Top-down survival, ~10-15 min session, day/night. Goal: survive 3 nights and light the Beacon (endgame) or just survive as long as possible? Add objective: gather 3 "ember shards" from ruins guarded, then light the Worldroot beacon. But for a demo, an open-ended survival with a "survive to dawn" rhythm and persistent escalation is fine. Include an objective meter to give direction: "Kindle the Beacon — collect 3 ember shards from the Hollow ruins and return to the Worldroot." Completing it triggers a "world remembers" epilogue and next cycle with higher difficulty.

Simplify: no crafting recipes tree? Crafting is core to survival. Implement 4 recipes: Axe (wood+stone), Spear (wood+flint), Torch (wood+fiber), Bandage (fiber+resin?) and Campfire (wood+stone) placeable. Also Cooked meat? Keep food as direct consume.

Combat: melee swing arc with equipped weapon, stamina cost; dodge roll i-frames. Enemies: wolves (fast, flank), hollows (raiders, ranged? maybe melee), and a night "Listener" mini-boss? Keep 3 enemy types: Wolf, Hollow, Warden (rare). Adaptive traits modify them.

Player attack styles tracked: weapon used (axe/spear/torch/bare), attack timing (spam vs charged), movement (kite/flee), engagement range, time of day, use of fire, stealth (sneaking), trap usage. This drives enemy adaptation:
- If fire damage high → "Fire-hardened" (fire resist, avoids torches).
- If spear used a lot at range → "Long-reach hunters" (close distance fast, shields).
- If player flees a lot → "Pursuers" (faster, more stamina).
- If player kills many wolves → "Wolves grow cunning" (pack flanking, avoid campfires).
- If player uses dodge a lot → "Feint attacks" (delayed strikes).
- If player fights at night → "Nightborn" (stronger at night).
- If player relies on campfire → "Ember-eaters" (extinguish fires).

Memory stored as numeric counters; derive traits each run; show in "The World Remembers" screen. Enemies with traits get visual cues (glowing eyes, scars, ash aura) and names.

NPCs: Worldroot camp with 2-3 NPCs: Maren the keeper, Sable the hunter, Fen the child? Dialogue adapts to reputation and history. They give quests (bring meat/wood), trade. If you attack them, they become hostile in future runs (remember betrayal). If you feed them, they leave gifts at camp next run. Persistent flags.

World persistence: burned trees stay burned, built campfires persist (maybe decay), graves of your past selves appear where you died with your old gear ("Remains of a past life" lootable). That's a killer feature: your previous death sites appear in the next run with a ghost marker and loot. Also your past runs' names/dates in chronicle.

Seeded world: seed derived from memory generation, so each run new layout but consistent within run.

Rendering quality: layered terrain with noise, animated water, grass tufts, trees with shadows, particles (embers, snow? no), dynamic day/night lighting overlay via offscreen lightmap with campfire/torch lights, fog of war/vignette, screen shake, damage numbers, blood particles, floating text. Camera follow with smoothing.

Audio: WebAudio procedural ambient pad + sfx (swing, hit, pickup, craft, night drone). Toggle mute. Keep subtle.

UI: 
- Title screen with animated background (ember particles, title, "The world remembers N cycles", Begin).
- HUD: HP/hunger/stamina bars, time/day, objective, inventory counts, equipped weapon, minimap.
- Craft panel (C) with recipes, clickable.
- Memory panel (Tab/M) with traits and chronicle.
- Death screen: "The world has learned" showing new traits, memories, and "Wake again".
- Dialogue overlay for NPCs.

Mobile: virtual joystick left, action buttons right (attack, interact, dodge), craft/menu buttons; responsive.

Testing: need playwright screenshots desktop/mobile. We'll write code, serve with python http.server on 3002 in tmux, then use playwright-cli. Must inspect screenshots visually.

This is a large amount of code. Let's plan files:

- index.html — markup + UI overlays
- css/style.css
- js/main.js — bootstrap, game loop, input
- js/world.js — noise, terrain gen, tiles, resources, collision, rendering world
- js/player.js
- js/enemies.js — AI + adaptation
- js/npc.js
- js/memory.js — persistent store, traits, chronicle
- js/ui.js — HUD updates, panels, dialogue, toasts
- js/audio.js
- js/render.js maybe merge into world.

Maybe simpler: 6 files ~3000 lines total. That's a lot of output tokens. I can write efficiently but need quality. Aim ~1800-2400 lines.

Alternative: Use a single JS file with sections — easier to keep coherent, but huge. Multiple modules is cleaner.

Let me think about architecture concretely.

### World
Tile size 48. World 160x160 tiles (7680 px). Terrain types: grass, forest floor, dirt, rock, water, sand, ash. Generate via value noise (seeded PRNG + fbm). Biomes: water lakes, rocky ridges, forests. Walkable except water and rock? Rock walkable? Make water impassable, cliffs impassable (rock walls). Trees are entities with collision.

Use tile-based collision grid computed from terrain + static props. Props: trees (wood), rocks (stone), bushes (fiber/berries), flint nodes, ruins (ember shards), campfire (player-built).

Rendering: only visible tiles. Pre-render terrain to offscreen canvas chunks? World 160x160*48 = 7680px canvas ~59M pixels, too big. Use chunk canvases 20x20 tiles rendered lazily. Or draw visible tiles each frame (~30x20=600 tiles) with simple shapes — fine. Add per-tile deterministic detail (grass blades) computed by hash. Draw cached per chunk maybe. 600 tiles * few ops okay at 60fps.

Lighting: draw scene, then a darkness overlay using 'multiply' composite with radial gradients punched out via 'destination-out' on an offscreen canvas, then draw overlay with 'source-over'? Standard: create lightCanvas same size; fill with night color (rgba dark blue with alpha), then globalCompositeOperation='destination-out' and draw radial gradients at light sources, then draw lightCanvas over main. That darkens everything except lights. Good.

Day/night: time 0..1 per day, dayLength ~180s. Night factor smooth. At night enemies spawn more, cold drains warmth? Skip warmth; use hunger + HP. Maybe "resolve" not needed.

### Player
pos, vel, radius, hp 100, hunger 100, stamina 100. Speed 200 px/s, sprint 300 with stamina. Attack: equipped weapon defines arc range, damage, cooldown, stamina. Dodge: 0.35s, i-frames, stamina 25.

Inventory: wood, stone, fiber, flint, berry, meat, shard, ember? Equipment: axe, spear, torch (toggle light), bandage count.

Interact E: nearest resource within radius or NPC or campfire. Auto-gather on hold? Use E to harvest (a few seconds?) Simple: press E near resource, yields instantly with cooldown and particles. Trees require axe for wood efficiency; rocks require... bare hands give less. Keep simple: each node has hp/harvests.

Hunger drains slowly; at 0 HP drains. Eat berries (E? use key F?) Simplify: auto-eat? No. Keys: 1 axe, 2 spear, 3 torch, 4 eat, Q bandage? Let's define:
- LMB / J: attack
- Space: dodge
- E: interact/harvest/talk
- 1-3: equip axe/spear/torch
- 4: eat
- 5: bandage
- C: craft
- M/Tab: memory
- Shift: sprint

Crafting recipes:
- Axe: 3 wood, 2 stone
- Spear: 3 wood, 1 flint, 1 fiber
- Torch: 2 wood, 2 fiber
- Bandage: 3 fiber
- Campfire: 5 wood, 4 stone (place at player)
- Cooked meat? skip, meat heals more when eaten near fire? nice but skip.

Ember shards: 3 ruins each guarded by Wardens; collect shard, return to Worldroot beacon. When 3 shards, interact with beacon to win cycle.

### Enemies
Types:
- Wolf: speed 190, hp 40, dmg 8, pack.
- Hollow: speed 120, hp 60, dmg 12, sometimes throws stone (ranged) — maybe keep melee with lunge.
- Warden: speed 90, hp 180, dmg 22, guards shard, telegraphed slam.

Spawning: at night, spawn offscreen near player based on danger; day fewer. Ruins have guards always. Population cap 12.

AI states: idle/wander, chase, attack windup, recover, flee (low hp). Wolves circle/flank. Adaptation modifies:
- speed multiplier, hp, damage
- fireResist
- dodgeRead (feint: windup longer but tracks player)
- packSize
- nightBuff
- ranged? 
Traits derived from memory with thresholds and displayed.

Learning tracked per encounter:
- damageByType {slash, pierce, fire, blunt}
- attacks, dodges, flees, kills, nightKills, campfireUses
- avgCombatDistance, sprintUse
Enemies "learn" during run too: adaptive meter increments when player uses same tactic repeatedly; e.g., after 5 fire hits, wolves start avoiding torch. Represent with a live "Adaptation" bar in HUD? Show toasts "The pack is learning your fire." Good.

### NPCs
Worldroot camp at world center-ish (fixed near spawn). NPCs: Maren (keeper, quests), Sable (hunter, trades), Pell (child, lore). Dialogue modal with choices? Keep simple: interact opens dialogue panel with lines and one action (give 3 meat → trust+, reward; ask about world → lore; trade?). Implement 2 quests:
- Maren: bring 3 berries → bandages + trust.

## Objective
- Build a playable browser game from the user's pitch: "An open-world survival game where the world remembers everything you do. NPCs adapt, enemies learn your strategies, and no two playthroughs are the same."

## Requirements
- No explicit requirements beyond the pitch; interpreted as a polished, self-contained browser survival game with persistent adaptive memory across runs.
- Must run offline in-browser, support desktop and mobile/touch controls.

## Decisions
- Built a 2D top-down canvas survival game (no Three.js/build step) named **The World Remembers**.
- Persistence via `localStorage` (`twr.memory.v1`): deaths create lootable cairns, burned trees persist, campfire ash persists, NPC trust/quests persist, derived enemy traits persist, chronicle survives cycles.
- Enemy adaptation derived from player combat style counters (fire/slash/pierce/blunt hits, dodges, fleeing, night kills, campfire use, wolf kills, NPC kills).
- NPC camp at the Worldroot with Maren, Sable, Pell; trust/quests/gifts and permanent death if attacked.
- 3 ruins with ember shards + Warden guards; collect 3 and kindle the Worldroot beacon to win a cycle.
- Day/night cycle (210s), hunger/stamina, crafting (axe/spear/torch/bandage/campfire), procedural 150×150-tile world regenerated each cycle from memory seed.

## Work State
### Completed
- Core game implemented: world generation, terrain/props, collision, player movement/combat/dodge, enemies (wolf/hollow/warden) with adaptation, NPCs/dialogue, crafting, inventory, day/night, lighting, particles, audio, title/death/victory/memory/craft screens.
- Persistent memory verified: deaths increment cycles, graves/cairns appear in later cycles, loot includes previous weapon, chronicle displays past deaths.
- Combat, gathering, crafting, death screen, new-cycle flow, and memory panel manually tested via Playwright.
- Mobile HUD partially fixed: smaller status/objective/clock, minimap 82px, mobile inventory repositioned above joystick.
- Title, gameplay, night, crafting, memory, death, and mobile screenshots captured in `screenshots/`.

- Title screen background still quite dark; could increase exposure / add embers.
